entries.title: Static Ogive Fairing and Swept Fin Launch Rocket
entries.description: One newly authored complete fictional non-weapon launch-rocket exterior. A single continuous tall stepped body runs from a full lower barrel through a real narrowed interstage waist and slimmer upper body into a flared broad fairing and smoothly changing pointed ogive nose. Integral face-material bands identify the waist without duplicated coincident plates. Four whole thick swept tail fins have long roots and finite flat lower tips. A separate thick downward-open blind bell has a real empty mouth and inner wall under the body. No old spacecraft cabin, landing legs, airplane fuselage, wing or propeller mesh is reused, resized, extracted or counted again. Unlike the old broad four-foot lander with cabin, side braces, footpads and ladder, this is an entire long axial launch-vehicle silhouette with a narrow stage waist and full upper fairing. Unlike the old horizontal three-wheel airplane, it has no cockpit canopy, transverse main wing, propeller or wheeled undercarriage. One static prop zero scenes; four opaque constant PBR materials, metres Z up, horizontal bounds-centred four-fin-tip ground datum. Fictional game-art proportions only, no real vehicle, insignia, text or brand. Decorative bell is not an engine. No internal fuel, combustion, pressure, guidance, stage separation, thrust, aerodynamics, flight, orbit, launch procedure, manufacture, installation, structural capacity or safety claim. Rigging, animation and interaction are not made or verified.

entries.title: Fixed Interleaved Scrolls And Open Chamber Display
entries.description: One newly authored complete fixed spiral-scroll chamber illustrative cutaway. A continuous thick circular casing and real annular backplate stand on two narrow feet and a common bed. Two separate full thick spiral ribbons wind inward between one another across visible radial gaps; each has complete front, back, inner, outer and end faces. Both are deliberately fixed into the common backplate and outer casing, not asserted to orbit independently. A central full spindle, proud front hub, rear bored bearing on its own pedestal and a rear cap complete the display. The new interleaved long spiral walls are not radial impeller blades in a single expanding volute, nor one curved triangular rotor inside a two-lobed casing. Generic numeric mesh/export routines only are reused; all visible profiles and placements are newly authored. Four opaque constant untextured PBR roles, metres and Z up; one model zero scenes. Illustrative static engineering-themed art only: not a working scroll compressor or conjugate scroll profile. No independent orbital mechanism, eccentric drive, fluid ports, chambers sealed through motion, compression, pumping, pressure, thermodynamics, flow, speed, precision, lubrication, manufacture, load or safety claim. Deliberate fixed support overlaps do not demonstrate working fits. No fluid, rig, animation or interaction.

entries.title: Fixed Long Barrel and Raised Clamp Curler
entries.description: One newly authored complete fixed clamp-barrel hair-curler appearance. A long contoured axial grip with blank control and a collar supports a complete blunt cylindrical barrel with a separate closed end cap. Beside it one thick concave spoon-shaped clamp is fixed visibly raised about a real transverse pin carried by two rooted ears; a full heel and reversed short thumb lever attach to that same hinge. The long curved clamp/barrel gap is real geometry, not a painted seam. Not the old iron removed from a solder station or the broad comb-headed clipper relabelled; all coordinates new. Three opaque materials, one prop zero scenes. Upright heel is a display datum only. No hair or person, sharp tip, heat, electricity, powered function, hinge sweep, spring, grooming procedure, suitability, ergonomics, hygiene or safety claim. Rigging animation interaction not made.

entries.title: Static Clinging Wedge-Bill Tail-Braced Woodpecker
entries.description: One newly authored complete stylised woodpecker-like bird in a fixed clinging pose on one short whole upright timber stem. Narrow upright torso flows into a short neck and small head with a long straight tapered wedge bill; two complete folded wings lie along the back, while two short bent legs meet full opposing-lobed thick feet against the stem and a long narrow stiff-looking tail reaches the lower stem. Whole new bird and stem construction together, not a recoloured hooked-bill standing parrot or a sloth branch with the animal swapped. The stem is a finite grounded pose support included in this single display model, not a separate tree asset. All visible forms are real closed thickness; no feather-strand, exact species, anatomical digit, climbing, pecking, balance, rig, animation, load or safety validation. One static model zero scenes.

entries.title: Whole Kiwi and Hollow Log Ground Margin
entries.description: One static ground-bird and hollow-deadwood margin scene, zero new models. Two complete qualified original objects remain unchanged at unit scale and with every original oriented world triangle and opaque per-face constant PBR: the irregular two-mouth split-window hollow fallen log spans the left-rear ground margin, and the entire low-body long-bill kiwi-like bird stands clear beside its right end on the open foreground side. A finite scene-only earth floor supports the entire original log sole and both original bird feet. The end mouth remains unobstructed and the bird is outside the log, not squeezed inside a shell or presented as a nesting animation. Unlike the earlier bank/reed shallow water sidepool, there is no water, bank module, reed barrier or crossing; the new relation is an intact ground animal beside a dry open deadwood edge with an empty forward strip. Neither old model is cropped, recoloured, scaled or split into parts; source normals/hierarchy are baked and flat normals recomputed, not claimed byte-identical. One scene zero new reusable models. Static artistic wildlife association only: no exact species co-occurrence, habitat suitability, animal care, foraging or nesting behavior, locomotion, biological process, navigation or safety claim.
